title: January 2016 CouncilStat hackathon at Civic Hall
shortLabel: Civic Hall and New York City Council event evidence
publicSummary: Civic Hall announced a January 30, 2016, 1-3 p.m. New York City Council hackathon focused on constituent services. A New York City Council event-day post located the gathering at Civic Hall and called it the Council's first CouncilStat hackathon. The Wayback page preserves the posts through an embedded social feed; it is not the event's calendar listing.
boundaries: Announced hours do not prove actual event duration.
Do not broaden first CouncilStat hackathon to first civic-data hackathon.

title: Recovered event branding
shortLabel: New York City Council Hackathon graphic
publicSummary: The Council-branded graphic attached to Civic Hall's announcement reads 'New York City Council Hackathon' and includes 'labs.council.nyc.' This is recovered promotional branding, not proof of a longer formal registration title.
boundaries: Do not infer a longer official title or the names of breakout tracks.

title: Independent development and press coverage of CallNYC
publicSummary: After CouncilStat constituent-services data became publicly available, Jamie independently developed CallNYC.org as a resident-facing civic-data prototype. Politico New York covered the project in March 2016. CallNYC was not an official Council product and is now an archived project.
boundaries: Do not say CallNYC was built at the hackathon.
Do not describe it as an official or current Council service.

title: Digital District breakout
publicSummary: Participant photographs document a breakout placard reading 'Digital District - Help improve City Council District office operations.'
boundaries: Treat Digital District as a breakout label, not the title of the entire event.
Do not publish until rights, crop, credit, and represented-person review are complete.
